events.title: The ransom of the kingdom

script.speaker: steward
script.text: My lord, the king has agreed to pay the Northmen four thousand pounds of silver to leave the kingdom, and the whole realm is to find it. Here is how it falls on us.

script.speaker: steward
script.text: You yourself are assessed at the army fine, by what you are worth: {tribute_866_personal}. That is the heavy part, and it must be in coin.

script.speaker: steward
script.text: Then every holding on your land pays: sixpence from each free manse, threepence from the servile, and word is there will be a second round of a penny more from every one of them before they have enough. That is {tribute_866_tenants} from our people altogether.

script.speaker: steward
script.text: And that is my worry, my lord. Fourpence is a piglet, or a pair of geese; most families can find it in an ordinary year. But they find it by carrying something to market, and this autumn every household between here and Chalon will be carrying the same eggs and cheeses and piglets to the same market in the same fortnight. Prices will be on the floor. Some will sell the breeding sow. Some will sell the seed corn, and we will both regret that in the spring.

script.speaker: chaplain
script.text: I will say what the bishops are saying, my lord, since you will hear it from them anyway: this is a disgrace. Four thousand pounds to heathens, melted out of altar plate, because the lords of this kingdom would not defend it by arms. I do not say it of you. I say it is being said.

script.speaker: steward
script.text: You have been saying for twenty years that paying them invites more, my lord. Here is your evidence, and every man in the county knows you said it first.

knows: The levy is assessed per recorded manse; an improved villa pays no more than a poor one, but it can produce coin on short notice.
Merchants pay a tenth of their goods; priests according to their means; each great lord collects from his own lands.
A count or royal vassal collects for his whole jurisdiction: honestly, harshly and keep the difference, or make up the shortfall himself.

events.title: The second ransom

script.speaker: steward
script.text: Again, my lord. Five thousand pounds this time, and only Francia and Burgundy are to find it; the Neustrians are paying off their own Northmen on the Loire and Lothair's old country is let off entirely. They have learned something since last time, though. The small people pay less: fourpence from a free holding, twopence from a servile. The rest comes from the rent, which is to say from us. A shilling from your own farm besides, and the priests are assessed as well.

script.speaker: steward
script.text: Less grief in the villages this time, my lord. More out of your purse.

script.speaker: steward
script.text: The count of it: {tribute_877_demesne} from the demesne, {tribute_877_rent} lost out of the rents, and the tenants find {tribute_877_tenants} between them.

knows: The 877 structure deliberately shifted the burden from tenants to lords; a lord who complains is complaining about a fairer tax.

choices.prompt: How does the villa meet the 877 levy?

Pay the tenants' share as well
Advance the tenants' share as a loan at interest

events.notes: The third block is engine-written to fill the amounts; the loan returns through tributes.ts. The cost of paying the tenants' share is folded into the lord's rent loss (the scripts: 'more out of your purse').

script.speaker: steward
script.text: The king has let a dozen new mints open since the recoinage, my lord. They needed the silver turned into pennies faster than ten towns could do it, what with the Northmen to pay.

script.speaker: steward
script.text: There's a moneychanger set up at the Autun market now, my lord, weighing coin and taking his cut. Pennies from across the Saône go light here, and ours go light there. Same silver, different names on it.

events.title: A mint of your own

script.speaker: steward
script.text: My lord, I'll say what others are thinking. Half the counts between here and the sea are striking their own pennies now, some by the king's leave and some by nobody's. We have the silver passing through, we have the market, and Chalon has had a mint since the old king's edict. It would pay well. And there is no one left in this kingdom with the strength to tell you no.

knows: Granted by the king: ask with service or silver behind it; easiest under Odo or Charles the Simple. No risk once granted.
Taken without permission: a usurpation of a royal right; a strong king or a stronger neighbour (Richard) can use it later.
Through a bishop or abbey: safe, slower, the church keeps the prestige and shares the profit.

hooks.trigger: The lord petitions the king for the right to strike coin, with service or silver behind the request.

hooks.trigger: The lord simply has coin struck in his own name.

events.notes: Count-rank only; the mint as a business (its income) belongs to the promotion pass. Costs are engine-chosen placeholders.

script.speaker: steward
script.text: Half the pennies in the district have a bishop's name on them now, or a count's. Nobody minds much. A penny is a penny if the weight is right, and a near lord stands behind it better than a far king.
